IGUI_KBW_GuideWelcomeBody: <H2> Welcome to Knox Buildworks <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Knox Buildworks gives you one organized place to discover, preview, plan, and construct buildings and objects. Open it from the building sidebar or with the configurable catalog key, which is F7 by default. It can live beside the vanilla Building Menu, or a server can make Knox the primary building action. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Build something <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> 1. Browse or search for what you want. <LINE> 2. Choose its quality, model, material, colour, or finish when those choices are available. <LINE> 3. Check what it needs and whether the current character is ready. <LINE> 4. Select Build to construct now, or Place Plan to leave a blueprint ghost for later. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> <GHC> Ready means your character passes the recipe checks shown in the catalog. <RGB:0.92,0.91,0.88> <SPACE> The placement cursor will then check the chosen location.
IGUI_KBW_GuideCatalogBody: <H2> Browse without guessing <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Categories and subcategories stay visible in the left sidebar. Search can look through recipe names, required items, or everything. The search scope, sort, material, skill, and All qualities controls stay above the catalogue; Clear filters returns to the full collection. Ready to build progressively finds recipes your character can make from carried and nearby ground supplies. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Fast navigation <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> Favorites keeps hand-picked recipes together. <LINE> Recent returns to recipes used lately. <LINE> Sorting changes the order without changing availability. <LINE> Grid and list buttons change density without losing the current selection. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> <IMAGE:media/ui/inventoryPanes/FavouriteYes.png,20,20> The star changes only your personal favorite list. A server-disabled buildable remains unavailable even when it is a favorite. <LINE> <LINE> Right-click a world tile and choose Find this piece in Knox Buildworks to open its recipe. For an empty opening, Find doors/windows for this opening lists compatible pieces, so matching a door or window no longer depends on guessing from the artwork.
IGUI_KBW_GuideViewsBody: <IMAGE:media/ui/craftingMenus/Icon_Grid.png,24,24> <SPACE> <IMAGE:media/ui/craftingMenus/Icon_List.png,24,24> <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Choose the view that suits you <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Grid view gives each buildable a visual card. List view fits more recipe names and readiness information on screen. In the normal window, the selected recipe stays in the right inspector and the magnifier on a card opens its larger preview. The rest of the card remains available for selection, favorites, and pins. <LINE> <LINE> Compact mode removes the fixed inspector to preserve world visibility. Rest the pointer on a compact card to see its preview, materials, tools, skills, and knowledge, then use the Build or Place Plan actions along the bottom. <LINE> <LINE> Recipes with several related pieces use the arrows in the inspector; the number between them shows the current member of the group. Drag the bottom-right corner to choose a comfortable size. The layout adapts to the current font and available space.
IGUI_KBW_GuideChoicesBody: <H2> Families instead of duplicate recipes <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Related pieces are often gathered into one buildable family. Use the arrows to move between roof shapes, wall pieces, furniture models, directions, or construction qualities instead of searching for a separate entry for every sprite. <LINE> <LINE> Material, colour, model, and finish selectors appear when that family supports them. The preview and requirements follow your selection, and the same choice is remembered when you place a plan. <LINE> <LINE> <PUSHRGB:0.88,0.78,0.40> Check the preview before placing. <POPRGB> <SPACE> Members of one family may have different dimensions or may need a wall, floor, frame, or open space.
IGUI_KBW_GuideDetailsBody: <H2> Reading the inspector <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> The fixed right-hand inspector shows the selected name, description, preview, useful properties, dimensions, readiness, and choices. Materials & Tools and Skills & Knowledge remain in the same inspector, each with its own scrolling area. Counts show what the character has and what the recipe needs. <LINE> <LINE> Select any requirement to open Available Ingredients / Possible Items at the far right. Owned alternatives are counted and marked there, and choosing one changes only that recipe input. The buildable list and selected recipe remain visible. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Storage capacity <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Storage is shown for one usable face instead of repeating the same information for every rotation. Multi-tile objects list every tile that provides storage, while appliances can list separate compartments such as Fridge and Freezer. Previewed capacity describes the finished object; a blueprint ghost cannot hold items.
IGUI_KBW_GuideReadinessBody: <IMAGE:media/ui/craftingMenus/BuildProperty_Book_16.png,20,20> <SPACE> <IMAGE:media/ui/craftingMenus/BuildProperty_Light_16.png,20,20> <SPACE> <IMAGE:media/ui/craftingMenus/BuildProperty_Clock_16.png,20,20> <LINE> <LINE> <H2> What Ready checks <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Materials, retained tools, drained uses, skills, learned recipes, light, reach, stage rules, and server availability can all affect readiness. Counts show available versus required amounts. Alternatives are grouped so any permitted item or tag can satisfy that input. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Requirement types <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> Consumed items disappear when used. <LINE> Retained tools must be present but are normally kept. <LINE> Drainable inputs remove uses rather than the entire item. <LINE> Destroyed inputs are deliberately removed by the recipe. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> <BHC> Ready in the catalog is guidance, not a promise that every world square is valid. <RGB:0.92,0.91,0.88> <SPACE> Placement performs the final world and server checks. Fading unavailable icons can be turned off in Knox UI Appearance without changing any rule.
IGUI_KBW_GuideMagazinesBody: <IMAGE:media/ui/craftingMenus/BuildProperty_Book_16.png,20,20> <LINE> <LINE>  <H2> Unlocking buildables <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Many buildables must be learned before they can be built. Read the matching magazine - such as Fine Wood Working, The Family Handyman, Old House Journal, Architectural Digest, Popular Mechanics, Home Mechanix, Projects In Metal, the Flooring Guide or the Decoration Guide - or reach the higher skill level the recipe allows instead. In Skills & Knowledge, select the knowledge row to see which magazine teaches it. <LINE> <LINE> Locked recipes are hidden until learned. All qualities shows them so you can see what a magazine unlocks, but they still cannot be built until you know them; the server checks the same rule. <LINE> <LINE>  <H2> Where to find them <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Magazines turn up in bookshops, libraries, magazine racks and mechanic shelves. Each one teaches one group of recipes, for example dressers, doors and windows, wooden floors, lighting or bathroom appliances. <LINE> <LINE>  <H2> Building components <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Appliances and plumbing use Refrigerant Bottles, Refrigerator Compressors, Plastic Sheets, Insulation Foam, Small Rubber Tubes, Thin Copper Pipe and Rubber Seals. They are found in tool and electronics stores and tool crates. Cut a Plastic Sheet into small sheets with scissors, make a Small Rubber Tube from a rubber hose, and assemble a Refrigerator Compressor from sheet metal, electronics scrap, electric wire, screws and thin copper pipe.
IGUI_KBW_GuideBuildingBody: <H2> Using the construction cursor <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Select Build, move the preview to the desired square, rotate or change its face when available, and confirm on a valid location. Many compatible buildables stay on the cursor so you can place several in a row while materials remain available. Right-click cancels placement; the catalogue returns on the next game update instead of reopening inside the cursor callback. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> If the preview is invalid <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Read the message beside the cursor. Look for occupied tiles, missing support, the wrong wall edge, a required floor or matching frame, poor light, distance, or something blocking a multi-tile footprint. Stairs, gates, large furniture, and irregular objects need every tile in their footprint to be valid. <LINE> <LINE> When the timed action finishes, the recipe uses its materials, keeps or wears its tools as described, awards its XP, and creates the finished object.
IGUI_KBW_GuideFinishesBody: <H2> Before and after construction <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> A material or finish selector changes the planned construction variant. Supported world actions can later apply plaster, paint, signs, or other finishes to a finished target. Each action still checks its normal tools, resources, skills, and target type. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Paintable objects <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Paintable furniture uses the object's custom color, matching the vanilla painting approach. White military crates are the neutral color base; green and gray military crates are also recognized by the Knox painting system. <LINE> <LINE> <PUSHRGB:0.88,0.78,0.40> Painting changes appearance only. <POPRGB> <SPACE> It does not alter container capacity, construction XP, recipe requirements, collision, or ownership.
IGUI_KBW_GuideFunctionalBody: <H2> More than decoration <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Storage furniture, fridges and freezers, doors, windows, lights, curtains, work surfaces, appliances, wells and other supported objects keep the gameplay functions appropriate to them after construction. Multi-tile storage can provide a container on more than one tile, while one appliance tile can have separate compartments such as Fridge and Freezer. <LINE> <LINE>  <H2> Lights, glass and curtains <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> A wall light switch built in a map house controls that house's room lights. Built in your own building, it switches itself together with the mains-powered lamps and ceiling lights in the same walled room. Either way it needs electricity.  <LINE> Glass panels, such as the side of a sliding glass door or shop and diner glass, are real locked glass: they block the way and can only be smashed.  <LINE> Built curtains open and close like vanilla curtains. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE>  <H2> Water wells <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Depending on the server settings, built wells either provide an unlimited source of clean water or hold a limited supply that slowly returns through groundwater and rain. If a limited well is empty, give it time or wait for rainfall.
IGUI_KBW_GuidePinnedBody: <IMAGECENTRE:media/ui/inventoryPanes/Button_Pin.png,28,28> <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Keep requirements visible <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Select the pin on a buildable to keep its recipe visible after the catalog closes. The pinned panel updates readiness, materials, tools, skills, and learned-recipe knowledge as the character and inventory change. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Pinned panel options <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Collapse individual recipes, move the panel when manual positioning is selected, and use its gear menu for alignment, position mode, opacity, accent bar, and icon or text presentation. <LINE> <LINE> Pinned recipes are a client convenience. They do not reserve items, start a queue, or change the server recipe.
IGUI_KBW_GuidePlanningBody: <H2> Two focused windows <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Open Planning Mode with the Plans button at the top of the catalogue. It keeps the blueprint workspace on the left and opens a separate, narrow buildable catalogue on the right. The workspace has four tabs: Plans, Pieces, Rooms and Supplies. The planning catalogue has search plus Category and Subcategory selectors, a compact buildable grid and arrows for group, variant, material and finish choices. Rest the pointer on a card to see its picture, materials, tools and skills beside the panel; Add to plan puts the chosen piece on the cursor. <LINE> <LINE>  <H2> Plans tab <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> A blueprint holds your planned pieces, rooms and gather area. Use New, Rename and Duplicate to manage plans, Show ghosts to draw the selected plan in the world (select it again to hide them), and Pin to follow the plan in the pinned recipes panel. Export, Import, Copy JSON, Manage access and Delete are also here (under More actions on smaller screens). Ghost opacity sets how strongly planned pieces are drawn. <LINE> <LINE>  <H2> Levels <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> A plan works on one level at a time. Use -Z and +Z to change the planning level, or Use my level to jump to the floor your character stands on. Ghosts, rooms and tools follow the selected level, so you can plan an upper storey from the ground. <LINE> <LINE>  <PUSHRGB:0.88,0.78,0.40> Planning never spends materials. <POPRGB> <SPACE> Ghosts provide no collision, storage, water, light or protection until they are constructed.
IGUI_KBW_GuidePlanningToolsBody: <H2> Adding pieces <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> Choose a piece in the planning catalogue, select Add to plan and click in the world. Walls drag in a line and floors fill a dragged rectangle.  <LINE> Quickbar: the numbered bar at the bottom of the screen saves the current catalogue selection with its stage, variant, material and finish. Click an empty slot to save it, click a filled slot or press 1-9 to place it, and right-click a slot to replace or clear it.  <LINE> Pipette: in the Pieces tab, select Pipette and hover a planned ghost or a built piece in the world. The piece that would be picked is outlined and named; when several share a tile, the rotate key steps through them. Click to keep planning with exactly that piece - recipe, variant, material, direction and paint, plaster or wallpaper - without searching the catalogue. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE>  <H2> Editing the plan <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> Select ghosts: drag a box to select planned pieces; hold Shift to add to the selection. Ctrl-click and Shift-click in the Pieces list select several pieces too.  <LINE> Delete selected, or the Delete key, removes every selected ghost at once.  <LINE> Erase tool removes the topmost planned piece on the tile you click; click again for the next one.  <LINE> Move blueprint shows the whole plan under the cursor and moves it where you click.  <LINE> Stop tool puts away whichever planning tool is in your hand. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE>  <PUSHRGB:0.88,0.78,0.40> A red ghost explains itself. <POPRGB> <SPACE> Hold the cursor over the spot to read why: another planned piece in the way, outside the plan's range, a missing frame or earlier stage, or no permission.
IGUI_KBW_GuideRoomsBody: <H2> Drawing rooms <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> In the Rooms tab, type a name, pick a colour, select Draw room and drag a rectangle on the planning level. Rooms mark out spaces, show as coloured outlines and give the Roof helper its footprint. <LINE> <LINE>  <H2> Any shape <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> Extend room: select a room and drag a rectangle that touches or overlaps it to add a wing; repeat for L, T, U or irregular shapes.  <LINE> Cut from room: select a room and drag an area to clear it out, for notches, holes or trimming a side. A room cut down to nothing is removed.  <LINE> Update room saves a new name or colour, Delete room removes the selected room, and Erase room removes the room on the tile you click. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> Rooms are planning marks only: they do not build walls or floors by themselves.
IGUI_KBW_GuideRoofsBody: <H2> Roofs without guesswork <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Select a room in the Rooms tab and open Roof helper. Neighbouring rooms on the same level are roofed together, and a room under an upper storey is roofed against that wall. The helper lists every roof that fits - flat, shed, lean-to, gable, hip and cross-gable - as small shaded 3D models, best first, with the recommended one marked. <LINE> <LINE>  <H2> Choosing a roof <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> Roof family and pitch: the roof tiles and their slope, 30 or 45 degrees.  <LINE> Gable walls and Gable finish: the end walls, in any variant their family shares and in paint, plaster, plaster with paint or wallpaper where every piece accepts it.  <LINE> Overhang, Maximum rise, Start level offset, Ceiling deck and Eaves fine-tune the roof.  <LINE> Hover a layout to see it in the world in its real tiles, click to choose it, then select Add preview to blueprint. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> The roof is added as ordinary planned pieces, so it is built, erased and checked like any other ghost. Shallow sheets, roof trim and tents are placed by hand from the catalogue. <LINE> <LINE>  <PUSHRGB:0.88,0.78,0.40> At 45 degrees the north and west slopes are hidden by the camera. <POPRGB> <SPACE> The ceiling deck keeps those tiles dry, as in vanilla buildings; at 30 degrees every side is built.
IGUI_KBW_GuidePreviewBody: <H2> World preview settings <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> In the Plans tab, World preview settings choose how ghosts are drawn: Blueprint tint, Original textures or Solid preview (100%). Show the selected level only, the selected level with faded neighbours, the selected level and below, or all levels, and hide roofs, planned walls or room zones while you work inside a building. These settings change only what you see and are kept per player. <LINE> <LINE>  <H2> Preview layout <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Preview layout opens the whole plan in its own window. Switch between Isometric and Top-down, move between floors, toggle the grid, use Fit, zoom with the mouse wheel and drag to pan. The top-down view draws walls on the edge they stand on, floors as filled squares, objects as blocks and roofs hatched, with north up; rooms keep their colours and the gather area has a green outline.
IGUI_KBW_GuideQueueBody: <H2> Checking supplies <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> The Supplies tab totals what the whole plan needs against what you have: carried items, bags in containers and on the ground, materials lying near the pieces, the gather area and vehicles. Shared ingredients are allocated across the plan and retained tools are counted once. Build all stays unavailable until the check is finished and the plan is ready. <LINE> <LINE>  <H2> Gather area <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Contributors can drag a Gather area in the Supplies tab. Containers and vehicles inside it are searched for construction resources. The area belongs to the blueprint and can be redrawn. <LINE> <LINE>  <H2> Building a plan <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> Build tool: click planned pieces in the world to build them one at a time.  <LINE> Build, in the Pieces tab, builds the piece selected in the list.  <LINE> Build all queues the ready ghosts and works through them; Stop queue cancels what is left. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> The character walks to the supplies, fetches what each piece needs and builds it. Materials lying beside a planned piece are used where they lie. Each construction still performs readiness, reach, placement, permission and server checks. <LINE> <LINE>  <PUSHRGB:0.88,0.78,0.40> The queue does not create missing resources or bypass locked recipes. <POPRGB> <SPACE> If it stops, inspect the next ghost, the inventory, the gather area, the path and your permissions.
IGUI_KBW_GuideSharingBody: <H2> Building together <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> A blueprint owner can keep a plan private or give access to everyone, a faction, or individual players. View access lets someone see the plan. Build access lets them construct its ghosts. Contribute access also lets them edit placements, rooms, and the gather area. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Taking a plan elsewhere <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> You can write a selected plan onto a supported in-game blueprint item and import a carried blueprint later. Planning Mode also provides local export and import controls for sharing a plan outside the game. An imported plan appears near the importing player so it can be moved into position. <LINE> <LINE> Access and ownership are not carried over as free permissions. The destination world or server still decides what the player may see, edit, and build.
IGUI_KBW_GuideAppearanceBody: <IMAGECENTRE:media/ui/inventoryPanes/Button_Gear.png,28,28> <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Knox UI Appearance <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> The gear opens personal display settings. Choose one of seven panel tones, enable high contrast, set panel opacity from 35% to 100%, and choose checkerboard, light, dark, or a custom object-preview background. Changes appear in the open catalogue while you make them and are saved for the next session. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Size and readability <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Card size ranges from 75% to 175%. Preview size has Default, Large, and Extra Large choices. Fade unavailable icons can be disabled when dimmed art is hard to recognize; readiness borders and building restrictions remain active. <LINE> <LINE> Grid, list, and compact modes control information density independently of these appearance choices. If you use a larger game font, resize the window or use compact mode for a smaller footprint. Appearance choices affect only your client.
IGUI_KBW_GuideMultiplayerBody: <H2> When one player cannot build <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Check that character's materials, tools, skills, learned recipes, light, distance, and blueprint access. Select the buildable again to read the missing requirement, then try the placement cursor on a suitable square. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> When everyone has the same problem <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Ask an administrator whether the buildable or its category was disabled and whether Planning Mode is allowed. Server and clients need matching Knox, ElyonLib, and enabled add-on versions. After a server or mod update, reconnect before testing again. <LINE> <LINE> Knox can be added to an existing save after making a complete backup. Do not remove it or an enabled construction add-on from a save that has loaded them: custom items and entities receive persistent WorldDictionary identities, so mid-save removal can prevent a world from loading. Restore the original mod set or a pre-installation backup instead of deleting dictionary files. <LINE> <LINE> <BHC> The server makes the final decision. <RGB:0.92,0.91,0.88> <SPACE> It checks the recipe, position, permissions, item use, XP, and finished object so every player sees the same result.
IGUI_KBW_GuideAdminRulesBody: <H2> Safe draft workflow <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Authorized administrators open Build Rules from the ElyonLib dock. The editor copies the synchronized server document into a private draft; browsing, loading a preset, and changing controls do not affect players. Validate and Save must succeed before the server publishes a new revision. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Editor layout <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Select a category, subcategory, or buildable on the left, then select a stage and tab on the right. Availability, inputs, finishes, skills and XP, recipe knowledge, and time are separate controls. The Finishes tab can waive plaster, paint, or wallpaper materials for every wall, while selected walls can explicitly inherit, require, or waive each cost. Non-wall paintable objects keep their normal requirements. Reload discards the draft and requests current server data. Reset Selected removes that buildable's overrides. <LINE> <LINE> Concurrent saves use revision checks. If another admin saves first, reload the newer revision before applying your changes.
IGUI_KBW_GuideAdminScopesBody: <H2> Category to buildable <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Availability is checked from category, to subcategory, to individual buildable. Inherit means that level follows the broader setting. A more specific choice can create an exception. <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> Disable a whole category when it does not fit the server. <LINE> Re-enable one useful subcategory inside it. <LINE> Disable or re-enable a single buildable for a final exception. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> The Effective Status line shows what players will actually receive. Use the broadest sensible rule first, then add only the exceptions you need.
IGUI_KBW_GuideAdminRecipesBody: <H2> Change only what your server needs <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Each build stage can have its own material and tool requirements, minimum skills, XP rewards, required learned recipes, and construction time. Turn on an override only for the part you want to replace; everything else continues to use the normal buildable recipe. <LINE> <LINE> Requirement rows let you choose valid items or tags, how many are needed, and whether they are consumed, kept, drained by uses, or destroyed. Use alternatives when several items should satisfy the same requirement. <LINE> <LINE> Select Validate and Save when finished. The editor will point out unknown items, recipes, skills, duplicates, and invalid values before anything is applied to players. Some special Build 42 objects keep protected native requirements, but their availability, XP, and build time can still be adjusted.
IGUI_KBW_GuideAdminPresetsBody: <H2> Starting points <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Current Server Rules reloads the rules players are using now. Definition Defaults returns the draft to the normal Knox recipes. Disable All is useful when you want to begin with a tightly restricted server and enable only selected groups. Loading any source changes only your draft. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Share and reuse a ruleset <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Give the preset a clear name and export it to your client. Another administrator can copy that preset into their own preset folder, select Import to refresh the list, and load it as a draft on another server. <LINE> <LINE> <BHC> Loading is not the same as applying. <RGB:0.92,0.91,0.88> <SPACE> Review the effective rules, select Validate and Save, and wait for the new server revision. Warnings usually mean that the preset expects buildables or add-ons that are not enabled here.
IGUI_KBW_GuideAdminSandboxBody: <H2> Menu and planning <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Replace vanilla Build Menu decides whether the sidebar Build button opens Knox Buildworks directly. Enable Planning Mode controls blueprint UI availability. Max planned buildables limits ghosts per blueprint, while Blueprint radius limits the square area around its first anchor. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Construction and water <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Build XP multiplier scales Knox construction awards. Water well supply selects infinite or limited-and-refilling behavior; limited mode also uses capacity, initial fill, groundwater-per-hour, and rain-refill settings. <LINE> <LINE> Sandbox options are separate from Build Rules. Use sandbox controls for global systems and limits; use Build Rules for category, subcategory, buildable, and stage policy.
IGUI_KBW_GuideAdminAuthorityBody: <H2> Rules are shared by the server <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> When an administrator saves a valid ruleset, connected players receive the new revision. The server then checks availability, requirements, placement, blueprint access, item use, XP, and the finished construction whenever somebody builds. A client preference cannot bypass those checks. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Keep the mod list consistent <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Enable the same Knox Buildworks version and construction add-ons for the server and every player. If an add-on is removed, review rules and presets that used its categories or buildables. Ask players to reconnect after changing the server mod list or applying a major update. <LINE> <LINE> Keep exported presets as backups before a large rules change, and test with a normal player rather than only an administrator account.
IGUI_KBW_GuideAdminToolsBody: <H2> Test Runner <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Use the Test Runner when an add-on or update introduces many buildables and you want a quick health check. Its filters help you find entries with missing sprites, incomplete stages, bad requirements, or unsupported special objects. Select a result to focus on the affected buildable. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Tile Browser <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> The Tile Browser lets you search the loaded tile library and inspect a sprite's visible properties. It is useful when a placed object behaves differently from its preview, when checking storage capacity, or when identifying the correct face of a multi-direction object. <LINE> <LINE> These tools help locate problems; always finish by placing and using the object in the actual world.
IGUI_KBW_GuideAdminAddonsBody: <H2> Core and Vanilla Expanded <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Knox Buildworks provides the system and its converted core construction. The included Vanilla Expanded add-on is optional and adds a much larger organized collection of walls, roofs, doors, windows, floors, fences, containers, furniture, decorations, vegetation, road pieces, and survival structures. <LINE> <LINE> Other compatible add-ons can place their buildables into the same catalog and reuse its categories. Enable only the collections wanted by the server, but remember that removing one also removes its recipes from searches, plans, and rule choices. <LINE> <LINE> For multiplayer, add each chosen construction add-on to both the server mod list and Workshop list, then ensure every player downloads the same version.
IGUI_KBW_GuideAdminWorkflowBody: <H2> A safe way to change server rules <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> 1. Reload Current Server Rules before editing. <LINE> 2. Export a named preset so you can return to the current setup. <LINE> 3. Prefer a category or subcategory rule when many related pieces need the same treatment. <LINE> 4. Use individual buildable and stage overrides only for exceptions. <LINE> 5. Review Effective Status and validate every edited section. <LINE> 6. Save and wait for the confirmation that a new revision was synchronized. <LINE> 7. Join as a normal player and try the affected recipes, plans, and permissions. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> If the result is not what you intended, reload the saved backup preset, review it, and apply it through Validate and Save.
IGUI_KBW_GuideAboutBody: <H2> A passion project for builders <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> I have always wanted Project Zomboid to offer a building experience where a large collection stays organized, choices are easy to understand, and an entire base can be planned before spending the first plank. That idea began with my Building Menu for Build 41. <LINE> <LINE> Build 42 changed construction and introduced a new vanilla Building Menu, but the planning tools, grouped choices, detailed recipe information, flexible presentation, and multiplayer controls I wanted were still outside what the vanilla menu offered. Rather than leave those ideas behind, I started again and built Knox Buildworks around them. <LINE> <LINE> This mod is my attempt to make building feel like a complete part of the game: browse naturally, understand what a recipe will do, design large projects, share them with friends, and give server communities meaningful control without losing the fun of construction. <LINE> <LINE> <PUSHRGB:0.88,0.78,0.40> <SPACE> Knox Buildworks is made for the community and continues to grow through player feedback. <POPRGB> <SPACE> If you enjoy the mod and would like to support the time that goes into it, the button below opens my Ko-fi page. Support is always optional, and playing, reporting problems, and sharing the mod are appreciated too.
IGUI_KBW_Drum_PutOutFirst: Put the fire out and clear the fuel first.
IGUI_KBW_BuildFirst: Build first: %1, on the same tile and facing the same direction.
IGUI_KBW_WindowFitHelp: Requires a matching window opening. Right-click an empty frame and choose "Find doors/windows for this opening".
IGUI_KBW_FindWorldPiece: Find this piece in Knox Buildworks
IGUI_KBW_FullHeightWindowFitHelp: Fits a full-height window opening, such as Clapboard Full Height Window Wall. Build the wall frame first, then the full-height opening. Right-click the opening to find matching windows.
IGUI_KBW_QuickbarAssign: Save catalogue selection in this slot
IGUI_KBW_QuickbarHelp: Click or press 1-9 to select. Right-click to save or clear. Saves stage, material, variant and finish.
IGUI_KBW_QuickbarUnavailable: This saved buildable is unavailable or locked. Check its knowledge and server settings.
IGUI_KBW_RoofLayouts: Roof layouts for this footprint (hover to preview in the world, click to choose)
IGUI_KBW_RoofComputing: Working out the roof layouts that fit this footprint.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_gable: Two slopes meet at the ridge; end walls close both gable ends.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_hip: Slopes on every side, with hips at the corners and valleys at inside corners. No end walls.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_crossGable: Each wing gets its own ridge, meeting the others in valleys; every wing ends in a gable wall.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_hipWings: The main block slopes on all sides; the wings end in gable walls.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_gableHipWings: The main block ends in gable walls; the wings are hipped.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_mixed: Some wings end in gable walls, the others are hipped.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_flat: A flat roof you can walk on.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_shed_S: One slope falling to the south, with a tall wall along the north side.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_shed_E: One slope falling to the east, with a tall wall along the west side.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_shed_N: One slope falling to the north, with a tall wall along the south side.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_shed_W: One slope falling to the west, with a tall wall along the east side.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_leanTo_S: Leans on the upper storey and falls to the south.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_leanTo_E: Leans on the upper storey and falls to the east.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_leanTo_N: Leans on the upper storey and falls to the north.
IGUI_KBW_RoofDesc_leanTo_W: Leans on the upper storey and falls to the west.
IGUI_KBW_RoofStats: %1 roof pieces, %2 end-wall pieces, %3 storey(s) high
IGUI_KBW_RoofTagCrown: Levels off into a flat crown after %1 storey(s).
IGUI_KBW_RoofTagApprox: %1 tile(s) use the closest piece this roof set has.
IGUI_KBW_RoofTagRidgeGap: This set has no ridge piece for an odd span; %1 ridge tile(s) stay open over the ceiling deck.
IGUI_KBW_RoofTagMissing: %1 visible tile(s) have no matching piece in this roof set.
IGUI_KBW_RoofSelectRoom: Select or draw a room in the Rooms tab first.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_covered_by_room: This room is covered by an upper room. Select its exposed upper floor to plan a roof.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_too_complex: These wings cannot form a clean pitched roof with the available pieces. Auto fit can cover the footprint with a continuous flat roof.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_missing_valley: This pitch has no verified corner or valley pieces for an automatic roof over this shape. Try 45° or use separate manual runs.
IGUI_KBW_RoofHelp: Every layout is drawn as a small model; the shading shows which way each slope faces. Hover a layout to see it in the world in its real tiles, click to choose it. Each card previews the real tile: use its arrows, the mouse wheel or a click on it to switch roof family, gable walls and gable finish (painted, wallpapered or plastered where the material allows it). At 45° the north and west slopes are hidden by the camera, so the ceiling deck keeps those tiles dry; at 30° both sides are built. End walls use the gable material and follow the exact slope of the roof. Only families the helper can lay out by itself are listed; shallow sheets, roof trim and tents are placed from the catalogue.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_no_profile: No unlocked roof family is available. Enable Vanilla Expanded and learn a matching magazine or skill.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_dimensions: Use a room with whole, positive dimensions and an overhang from 0 to 2.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_too_large: The roof helper supports up to 576 tiles including overhang. Divide a larger footprint into rooms.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_unsupported_shape: This shape cannot make a continuous roof with the chosen pitch, direction and footprint. Try another layout or divide the footprint.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_missing_face: This family lacks a required slope face or step. Select another direction, pitch or family.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_missing_slope: This family has no supported slope sequence. Select a pitched family or a flat roof.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_missing_flat: This family has no matching flat roof tile. Select another family.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_odd_gable: This family has no automatic ridge for an odd span. Use an even span, a flat cap, or place its ridge pieces manually.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_height_limit: The roof would exceed the supported world height.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_no_permission: You need contribute access to edit this blueprint.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_placement_limit: This roof would exceed the blueprint placement limit.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_out_of_range: The roof extends beyond the blueprint planning area.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_plan_overlap: The roof overlaps existing planned pieces. Adjust the footprint or remove conflicting plans first.
IGUI_KBW_FetchCapacityBlocked: There are matching supplies, but none can be carried or transferred. Free space in your inventory or backpack, or place materials beside the build site.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_locked: A required roof piece is locked or disabled. Choose an unlocked family or refresh the helper after learning its requirements.
IGUI_KBW_RoofAutoComplex: This footprint has %1 crossing wings, so Auto fit selected a continuous flat roof.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_manual_only: This family contains individually placed roof details, not a complete automatic roof. Use Place roof detail.
IGUI_KBW_RoofNoSuggestions: No complete layout for these options. Change the family or clear optional additions.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_missing_hip: This family has no complete automatic hip mapping. Its hip pieces are available under Place roof detail.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_missing_eaves: Matching automatic eaves are unavailable for this family. Turn eaves off or place its details manually.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_eaves_shape: Flat roofs have no authored edge eaves. Turn eaves off or place trim manually.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_rise_shape: A flat roof has no slope to cap. Set maximum rise to Full Rise.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_missing_gable: A matching gable slope, end or full-height wall is locked or unavailable. Choose another gable family or omit gable walls.
IGUI_KBW_RoofError_gable_shape: Gable end walls require Gable, Cross gable or Hip with gabled wings. Choose one of those layouts or set gable material to None.
IGUI_KBW_RoofAutoValley: This footprint turns through a valley angle missing from this roof set. Auto fit chose a continuous flat roof.
IGUI_KBW_RoofAutoSkippedDetails: The safe flat layout omits the selected pitched-roof eaves or gable walls. Choose a supported pitched layout if you need those details.
